messages:
hana: Hi folks, first-day snag. I accepted the org invite and enabled 2FA, but VS Code's GitHub extension still shows me as outside-collab and I can't push to private repos. Browser shows I'm a member of the org. Anyone seen this with VS Code?

it-bot: Org policy requires SAML SSO + 2FA. Some OAuth apps (VS Code extension, GitHub Desktop) need you to re-authorize after SSO. See https://github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/sso :robot_face: 

dev-adv: welcome @hana! Two quick checks: 1) which account is VS Code signed into (work vs personal), 2) are you using a fine-grained PAT or the OAuth flow? VS Code sometimes caches a token from a personal account.

hana: I'm signed into VS Code with my work account (hana@redwood.com) but the extension auth prompt previously accepted my personal account. I did create a fine-grained token yesterday for a personal project. Could that be interfering?

ops: Yes, fine-grained PATs created under a personal account won't be valid for org repos if SSO blocks external tokens. If VS Code is using that token, pushes will be denied. Run `git remote -v` and `gh auth status` to see which creds are active.

hana: `gh auth status` shows: 
```
github.com: Logged in to github.com as hana (Work account)
Git operations for github.com: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-demo (permission: none)
```

maya: That permission: none line means the CLI/VS Code isn't presenting the work credentials to git ops. Try this: in VS Code sign out of GitHub extension, then in browser open https://github.com/settings/applications and remove any GH for VS Code tokens from your personal account. Then re-run `gh auth login` and use the browser OAuth flow while signed into your work account, and re-authorize the redwood-inference org.

hana: did that. Also found an old PAT in ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml for github.com pointing to my personal account token. Deleted it and re-ran `gh auth login`.

ops: After refreshing auth, also restart VS Code so the extension picks up the new token. If you still see 403 on push, run `GIT_TRACE=1 GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -v" git push` and paste the relevant lines.

hana: restarted VS Code, re-authorized, clicked the SSO banner on the org page. Now `git push` succeeds. Thanks!

welcome-bot: Welcome to Redwood, hana! :tada: If you used personal tokens/apps, note the onboarding checklist addition: remove cached personal tokens, use `gh auth login` with work account, re-authorize org SSO, restart editor.

dev-adv: One extra tip: if you keep both personal and work accounts, use separate browser profiles + VS Code profiles to isolate OAuth sessions. Also `gh auth status --show-token` helps debug which token CLI is using.

hana: saved those notes and added a short paragraph to my onboarding doc about VS Code token gotchas. Appreciate the help :heart:
